children: Shares of Reliance Industries Ltd. (RIL) will be in focus on Monday, November 2, after the conglomerate reported its strongest-ever quarterly performance, with record revenue and a sharp improvement in profitability in the September quarter.
The company's consolidated profit after tax (PAT) for the first half of FY27 also crossed the ₹50,000 crore mark.

On a sequential basis, RIL's revenue increased to ₹3.62 lakh crore from ₹3.4 lakh crore in the previous quarter. EBITDA rose to ₹62,409 crore from ₹54,067 crore, while operating profit margin (OPM) improved to 18.8% from 17.3%.
Net profit for the quarter stood at ₹29,550 crore, compared with ₹23,196 crore in the June quarter.
O2C business delivers strong performance
The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business emerged as a key growth driver, with EBITDA increasing 67% sequentially to ₹25,203 crore, significantly ahead of the estimated 20% growth.

O2C EBITDA margin expanded to 10.8% from 8.4% in the previous quarter. The company attributed the improvement to stronger transportation fuel cracks, which were 3-3.7 times higher year-on-year and touched historic highs.
Margins across the polyester chain also reached a three-year high.
Oil and gas business

The oil and gas segment reported revenue of ₹6,020 crore, compared with ₹6,298 crore in the previous quarter. EBITDA came in at ₹4,901 crore against ₹4,973 crore in the June quarter, while OPM improved to 81.4% from 79%.
The company said lower production and realisations from the KG-D6 gas fields were offset by improved volumes and pricing in its coal-bed methane (CBM) business.
Reliance Retail performance
Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd. (RRVL) reported gross revenue of ₹91,716 crore, registering 6.4% year-on-year growth, adjusted for the demerger of the Consumer Brands business.
The company said the performance was impacted by the shift in the festive calendar to the December quarter.
EBITDA, before a one-time impairment charge, stood at ₹6,228 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 7.8%.
Jio continues to report growth
Reliance Jio's operating revenue increased to ₹40,475 crore from ₹39,173 crore in the previous quarter and ₹36,332 crore in the year-ago period.
Average revenue per user (ARPU) improved to ₹218.80 from ₹215.60 in the June quarter and ₹211.40 in the corresponding quarter last year.
The company attributed the growth in Jio Platforms' revenue to subscriber additions, higher ARPU and healthy growth in digital services.
What Nuvama Institutional Equities said

Brokerage firm Nuvama Institutional Equities maintained its 'Buy' rating on Reliance Industries but lowered its target price to ₹1,703 from ₹1,766, factoring in a 25% holding company discount following Jio's listing.

The brokerage said RIL is currently trading at 18 times its estimated FY28 earnings per share (EPS). It also highlighted the company's relatively modest net debt of ₹1.17 lakh crore, down 1% year-on-year, as a factor keeping its weighted average cost of capital (WACC) in check.
Nuvama said its 'Golden Refining Era' thesis, which anticipates sustainable gross refining margins (GRMs) of more than $10 per barrel, remains intact.

The brokerage expects the New Energy (NE) business rollout to contribute more than 50% to PAT over time and potentially drive a valuation re-rating. It also sees potential valuation benefits for the O2C business from the company's net-zero carbon target by 2035.
However, Nuvama lowered its FY27 and FY28 EBITDA estimates by 1% each, citing weakness in the retail business.

Of the 31 analysts tracking Reliance Industries, 30 have a 'Buy' recommendation on the stock, while one has a 'Sell' rating. The consensus price target indicates a potential upside of 39% from current levels.

title: Reliance Industries share price may rise 39% as per consensus estimates; check targets after Q2
